sanskrit: eṣa krodhavaśān hatvā parvate gandhamādane saugandhikāni divyāni kṛṣṇārthe samupāharat
english: This one, overcome by rage, slew [them] on the Gandhamādana mountain and brought back divine saugandhika flowers for Kṛṣṇā's sake.

sanskrit: gandharva eṣa vai hantā kīcakānāṃ durātmanām vyāghrān ṛkṣān varāhāṃś ca hatavān strīpure tava
english: This one is indeed the slayer of the wicked Kīcakas — and it was he who killed tigers, bears, and boars in your women's quarter.

sanskrit: yaś cāsīd aśvabandhas te nakulo 'yaṃ paraṃtapaḥ gosaṃkhyaḥ sahadevaś ca mādrīputrau mahārathau
english: He who was your horse-keeper is this Nakula, the scorcher of foes; and Sahadeva was the cattle-counter — both sons of Mādrī, both great warriors on the chariot.

sanskrit: śṛṅgāraveṣābharaṇau rūpavantau yaśasvinau nānārathasahasrāṇāṃ samarthau puruṣarṣabhau
english: Adorned in ornaments of beauty, handsome, renowned, capable of handling thousands of diverse chariots — these two are bulls among men.

sanskrit: eṣā padmapalāśākṣī sumadhyā cāruhāsinī sairandhrī draupadī rājan yatkṛte kīcakā hatāḥ
english: This lotus-petal-eyed one, slender-waisted, lovely-smiling — she is Draupadī the sairandhrī, O king, on whose account the Kīcakas were slain.

sanskrit: arjuno 'haṃ mahārāja vyaktaṃ te śrotram āgataḥ bhīmād avarajaḥ pārtho yamābhyāṃ cāpi pūrvajaḥ
english: I am Arjuna, O great king — I have now clearly come to your ears. I am Pārtha, younger than Bhīma and elder than the two Yamas' sons.

sanskrit: uṣitāḥ sma mahārāja sukhaṃ tava niveśane ajñātavāsam uṣitā garbhavāsa iva prajāḥ
english: We have lived happily, O great king, in your abode, dwelling unrecognized like creatures dwelling in a womb.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca yadārjunena te vīrāḥ kathitāḥ pañca pāṇḍavāḥ tadārjunasya vairāṭiḥ kathayām āsa vikramam
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: When Arjuna had thus described those five Pāṇḍava heroes, the son of Virāṭa then recounted Arjuna's own feats of valor.

sanskrit: ayaṃ sa dviṣatāṃ madhye mṛgāṇām iva kesarī acarad rathavṛndeṣu nighnaṃs teṣāṃ varān varān
english: This one moved among the enemy's chariot-hosts like a lion among deer, striking down their foremost warriors one after another.

sanskrit: anena viddho mātaṅgo mahān ekeṣuṇā hataḥ hiraṇyakakṣyaḥ saṃgrāme dantābhyām agaman mahīm
english: By him a great elephant was pierced and slain with a single arrow; Hiraṇyakakṣya fell to the ground in battle, felled by his tusks.

sanskrit: anena vijitā gāvo jitāś ca kuravo yudhi asya śaṅkhapraṇādena karṇau me badhirīkṛtau
english: By him the cattle were recovered and the Kurus were defeated in battle; the blast of his conch made my ears go deaf.

sanskrit: tasya tad vacanaṃ śrutvā matsyarājaḥ pratāpavān uttaraṃ pratyuvācedam abhipanno yudhiṣṭhire
english: Hearing those words of his, the powerful king of the Matsyas, his heart inclined toward Yudhiṣṭhira, replied to Uttara thus:

sanskrit: prasādanaṃ pāṇḍavasya prāptakālaṃ hi rocaye uttarāṃ ca prayacchāmi pārthāya yadi te matam
english: I think it is the proper time to propitiate the Pāṇḍava, and I am willing to give Uttarā to Pārtha — if that is agreeable to you.

sanskrit: uttara uvāca arcyāḥ pūjyāś ca mānyāś ca prāptakālaṃ ca me matam pūjyantāṃ pūjanārhāś ca mahābhāgāś ca pāṇḍavāḥ
english: Uttara said: They are worthy of honor, of worship, of reverence — and it is my view that the time is right. Let the greatly fortunate Pāṇḍavas, who deserve all worship, be duly honored.

sanskrit: virāṭa uvāca ahaṃ khalv api saṃgrāme śatrūṇāṃ vaśam āgataḥ mokṣito bhīmasenena gāvaś ca vijitās tathā
english: Virāṭa said: I too fell into the enemy's power in battle and was rescued by Bhīmasena; and the cattle were likewise recovered.

sanskrit: eteṣāṃ bāhuvīryeṇa yad asmākaṃ jayo mṛdhe vayaṃ sarve sahāmātyāḥ kuntīputraṃ yudhiṣṭhiram prasādayāmo bhadraṃ te sānujaṃ pāṇḍavarṣabham
english: Whatever victory was ours in battle came through the might of their arms; therefore let all of us together with our ministers propitiate Yudhiṣṭhira, the son of Kuntī — good fortune to you — along with his brothers, that bull among the Pāṇḍavas.

sanskrit: yad asmābhir ajānadbhiḥ kiṃ cid ukto narādhipaḥ kṣantum arhati tat sarvaṃ dharmātmā hy eṣa pāṇḍavaḥ
english: Whatever was said to that lord of men by us who did not recognize him, this virtuous-souled Pāṇḍava ought to forgive it all.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tato virāṭaḥ paramābhituṣṭaḥ; sametya rājñā samayaṃ cakāra rājyaṃ ca sarvaṃ visasarja tasmai; sadaṇḍakośaṃ sapuraṃ mahātmā
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Then Virāṭa, supremely pleased, met with the king and made a pact with him, and the great-souled one surrendered to him his entire kingdom along with its treasury, army, and city.

sanskrit: pāṇḍavāṃś ca tataḥ sarvān matsyarājaḥ pratāpavān dhanaṃjayaṃ puraskṛtya diṣṭyā diṣṭyeti cābravīt
english: Then the powerful king of the Matsyas, placing Dhanaṃjaya at the fore, addressed all the Pāṇḍavas saying, 'Fortune! Fortune!'

sanskrit: samupāghrāya mūrdhānaṃ saṃśliṣya ca punaḥ punaḥ yudhiṣṭhiraṃ ca bhīmaṃ ca mādrīputrau ca pāṇḍavau
english: Smelling their heads and embracing them again and again — Yudhiṣṭhira, Bhīma, and the two sons of Mādrī —

sanskrit: nātṛpyad darśane teṣāṃ virāṭo vāhinīpatiḥ saṃprīyamāṇo rājānaṃ yudhiṣṭhiram athābravīt
english: Virāṭa, lord of the army, could not be sated with the sight of them; rejoicing greatly, he then spoke to king Yudhiṣṭhira:

sanskrit: diṣṭyā bhavantaḥ saṃprāptāḥ sarve kuśalino vanāt diṣṭyā ca pāritaṃ kṛcchram ajñātaṃ vai durātmabhiḥ
english: 'By good fortune you have all returned safe from the forest! By good fortune the hardship imposed by those wicked ones — the incognito year — has been completed!'

sanskrit: idaṃ ca rājyaṃ naḥ pārthā yac cānyad vasu kiṃ cana pratigṛhṇantu tat sarvaṃ kaunteyā aviśaṅkayā
english: 'Let the sons of Kuntī accept without hesitation this kingdom of ours and whatever other wealth there may be — let them take it all.'

sanskrit: uttarāṃ pratigṛhṇātu savyasācī dhanaṃjayaḥ ayaṃ hy aupayiko bhartā tasyāḥ puruṣasattamaḥ
english: 'Let the left-handed Dhanaṃjaya accept Uttarā; this best of men is the fitting husband for her.'

sanskrit: evam ukto dharmarājaḥ pārtham aikṣad dhanaṃjayam īkṣitaś cārjuno bhrātrā matsyaṃ vacanam abravīt
english: Thus addressed, the king of dharma glanced at Pārtha Dhanaṃjaya; and Arjuna, so regarded by his brother, spoke these words to Matsya:

sanskrit: pratigṛhṇāmy ahaṃ rājan snuṣāṃ duhitaraṃ tava yuktaś cāvāṃ hi saṃbandho matsyabhāratasattamau
english: 'I accept your daughter as a daughter-in-law, O king; the alliance between us two is fitting — the best of the Matsyas and the best of the Bharatas.'

sanskrit: virāṭa uvāca kimarthaṃ pāṇḍavaśreṣṭha bhāryāṃ duhitaraṃ mama pratigrahītuṃ nemāṃ tvaṃ mayā dattām ihecchasi
english: Virāṭa said: Why, O foremost of the Pāṇḍavas, do you not wish to take my daughter, offered by me, as your own wife here?

sanskrit: arjuna uvāca antaḥpure 'ham uṣitaḥ sadā paśyan sutāṃ tava rahasyaṃ ca prakāśaṃ ca viśvastā pitṛvan mayi
english: Arjuna said: I lived in the inner apartments always beholding your daughter, in private and in public, while she trusted me as a father.

sanskrit: priyo bahumataś cāhaṃ nartako gītakovidaḥ ācāryavac ca māṃ nityaṃ manyate duhitā tava
english: I was dear and highly regarded as a dancing-master skilled in song; your daughter always regarded me as a teacher.

sanskrit: vayaḥsthayā tayā rājan saha saṃvatsaroṣitaḥ atiśaṅkā bhavet sthāne tava lokasya cābhibho
english: O king, O lord, I dwelt a year together with her, a young woman of age; great suspicion would arise — rightly — in you and in the world.

sanskrit: tasmān nimantraye tvāhaṃ duhituḥ pṛthivīpate śuddho jitendriyo dāntas tasyāḥ śuddhiḥ kṛtā mayā
english: Therefore I ask this of you regarding your daughter, O lord of the earth: I am pure, my senses are conquered, self-restrained; her purity has been maintained by me.

sanskrit: snuṣāyā duhitur vāpi putre cātmani vā punaḥ atra śaṅkāṃ na paśyāmi tena śuddhir bhaviṣyati
english: Whether as daughter-in-law or as daughter, whether for a son or for myself — I see no doubt in this; by that arrangement her purity shall be established.

sanskrit: abhiṣaṅgād ahaṃ bhīto mithyācārāt paraṃtapa snuṣārtham uttarāṃ rājan pratigṛhṇāmi te sutām
english: I am afraid of impure attachment, O scorcher of foes, and of improper conduct; therefore, O king, I accept your daughter Uttarā as a daughter-in-law.

sanskrit: svasrīyo vāsudevasya sākṣād devaśiśur yathā dayitaś cakrahastasya bāla evāstrakovidaḥ
english: The nephew of Vāsudeva, like a divine child incarnate, beloved of the discus-wielder — though still a boy he is already versed in the science of weapons —

sanskrit: abhimanyur mahābāhuḥ putro mama viśāṃ pate jāmātā tava yukto vai bhartā ca duhitus tava
english: Abhimanyu of the great arms, my son, O lord of the people — he is indeed the fitting son-in-law for you and the proper husband for your daughter.

sanskrit: virāṭa uvāca upapannaṃ kuruśreṣṭhe kuntīputre dhanaṃjaye ya evaṃ dharmanityaś ca jātajñānaś ca pāṇḍavaḥ
english: Virāṭa said: This befits you, O best of the Kurus, O Dhanaṃjaya son of Kuntī — you who are thus ever steadfast in dharma and whose wisdom has arisen, O Pāṇḍava.

sanskrit: yatkṛtyaṃ manyase pārtha kriyatāṃ tadanantaram sarve kāmāḥ samṛddhā me saṃbandhī yasya me 'rjunaḥ
english: Whatever you think should be done, O Pārtha, let it be done forthwith; all my desires are fulfilled, since Arjuna is my kinsman by marriage.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca evaṃ bruvati rājendre kuntīputro yudhiṣṭhiraḥ anvajānāt sa saṃyogaṃ samaye matsyapārthayoḥ
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: As the king of kings spoke thus, Yudhiṣṭhira the son of Kuntī then gave his approval to the union between the Matsya and the Pārtha at the appointed time.

sanskrit: tato mitreṣu sarveṣu vāsudeve ca bhārata preṣayām āsa kaunteyo virāṭaś ca mahīpatiḥ
english: Then, O Bhārata, the son of Kuntī and Virāṭa, lord of the earth, sent messages to all their friends and to Vāsudeva.

sanskrit: tatas trayodaśe varṣe nivṛtte pañca pāṇḍavāḥ upaplavye virāṭasya samapadyanta sarvaśaḥ
english: Then, when the thirteenth year had passed, the five Pāṇḍavas assembled altogether at Upaplavya, in Virāṭa's territory.

sanskrit: tasmin vasaṃś ca bībhatsur ānināya janārdanam ānartebhyo 'pi dāśārhān abhimanyuṃ ca pāṇḍavaḥ
english: While residing there, Bībhatsu the Pāṇḍava brought Janārdana and the Dāśārhas from the Ānartas, and Abhimanyu as well.

sanskrit: kāśirājaś ca śaibyaś ca prīyamāṇau yudhiṣṭhire akṣauhiṇībhyāṃ sahitāv āgatau pṛthivīpate
english: The king of Kāśī and Śaibya, both devoted to Yudhiṣṭhira, came along with two akṣauhiṇī armies, O lord of the earth.

sanskrit: akṣauhiṇyā ca tejasvī yajñaseno mahābalaḥ draupadyāś ca sutā vīrāḥ śikhaṇḍī cāparājitaḥ
english: The splendid and mighty Yajñasena came with one akṣauhiṇī; the heroic sons of Draupadī came, and the unvanquished Śikhaṇḍī.

sanskrit: dhṛṣṭadyumnaś ca durdharṣaḥ sarvaśastrabhṛtāṃ varaḥ samastākṣauhiṇīpālā yajvāno bhūridakṣiṇāḥ sarve śastrāstrasaṃpannāḥ sarve śūrās tanutyajaḥ
english: The irresistible Dhṛṣṭadyumna, foremost of all who bear weapons, came; and all the commanders of the combined akṣauhiṇī forces — sacrificers who give lavish dakṣiṇā, all skilled in weapons and arms, all heroes ready to lay down their lives.

sanskrit: tān āgatān abhiprekṣya matsyo dharmabhṛtāṃ varaḥ prīto 'bhavad duhitaraṃ dattvā tām abhimanyave
english: Seeing them arrived, Matsya, best of those who uphold dharma, was filled with joy at having given his daughter to Abhimanyu.

sanskrit: tataḥ pratyupayāteṣu pārthiveṣu tatas tataḥ tatrāgamad vāsudevo vanamālī halāyudhaḥ kṛtavarmā ca hārdikyo yuyudhānaś ca sātyakiḥ
english: Then, as kings arrived from here and there, Vāsudeva wearing the forest-garland came there, and Halāyudha, and Kṛtavarmā the son of Hārdika, and Yuyudhāna Sātyaki.

sanskrit: anādhṛṣṭis tathākrūraḥ sāmbo niśaṭha eva ca abhimanyum upādāya saha mātrā paraṃtapāḥ
english: Anādhṛṣṭi and Akrūra, Sāmba and Niśaṭha likewise — those scorchers of foes came bringing Abhimanyu along with his mother.

sanskrit: indrasenādayaś caiva rathais taiḥ susamāhitaiḥ āyayuḥ sahitāḥ sarve parisaṃvatsaroṣitāḥ
english: Indrasena and the others too came together in those well-equipped chariots — all who had dwelt apart for the full year.

sanskrit: daśa nāgasahasrāṇi hayānāṃ ca śatāyutam rathānām arbudaṃ pūrṇaṃ nikharvaṃ ca padātinām
english: Ten thousand elephants, ten million horses, a full arbuda of chariots, and a nikh arva of infantry —

sanskrit: vṛṣṇyandhakāś ca bahavo bhojāś ca paramaujasaḥ anvayur vṛṣṇiśārdūlaṃ vāsudevaṃ mahādyutim
english: Many Vṛṣṇis and Andhakas and Bhojas of supreme vigor followed Vāsudeva, the tiger among the Vṛṣṇis, of great splendor.

sanskrit: pāribarhaṃ dadau kṛṣṇaḥ pāṇḍavānāṃ mahātmanām striyo ratnāni vāsāṃsi pṛthak pṛthag anekaśaḥ tato vivāho vidhivad vavṛte matsyapārthayoḥ
english: Kṛṣṇa gave bridal gifts to the great-souled Pāṇḍavas — women, jewels, and garments separately in great abundance; then the wedding between the Matsya princess and the Pārtha proceeded according to proper rite.

sanskrit: tataḥ śaṅkhāś ca bheryaś ca gomukhāḍambarās tathā pārthaiḥ saṃyujyamānasya nedur matsyasya veśmani
english: Then conches, kettle-drums, trumpets, and large drums resounded in the dwelling of Matsya as his alliance with the Pārthas was being celebrated.

sanskrit: uccāvacān mṛgāñ jaghnur medhyāṃś ca śataśaḥ paśūn surāmaireyapānāni prabhūtāny abhyahārayan
english: They slaughtered various deer and hundreds of sacrificially pure animals; copious drinks of surā and maireya liquor were brought forth.

sanskrit: gāyanākhyānaśīlāś ca naṭā vaitālikās tathā stuvantas tān upātiṣṭhan sūtāś ca saha māgadhaiḥ
english: Singers skilled in narrative, actors, and bards approached praising them; sūtas together with māgadhas attended upon them with eulogies.

sanskrit: sudeṣṇāṃ ca puraskṛtya matsyānāṃ ca varastriyaḥ ājagmuś cārusarvāṅgyaḥ sumṛṣṭamaṇikuṇḍalāḥ
english: Placing Sudeṣṇā at their head, the finest women of the Matsyas came — beautiful in every limb, their gem-earrings gleaming bright.

sanskrit: varṇopapannās tā nāryo rūpavatyaḥ svalaṃkṛtāḥ sarvāś cābhyabhavat kṛṣṇā rūpeṇa yaśasā śriyā
english: Those women, endowed with fine complexion, beautiful, well-adorned — yet Kṛṣṇā surpassed them all in beauty, fame, and glory.

sanskrit: parivāryottarāṃ tās tu rājaputrīm alaṃkṛtām sutām iva mahendrasya puraskṛtyopatasthire
english: Surrounding the adorned princess Uttarā — like the daughter of great Indra — they placed her at the fore and attended upon her.

sanskrit: tāṃ pratyagṛhṇāt kaunteyaḥ sutasyārthe dhanaṃjayaḥ saubhadrasyānavadyāṅgīṃ virāṭatanayāṃ tadā
english: The son of Kuntī, Dhanaṃjaya, then accepted her — the flawless-limbed daughter of Virāṭa — on behalf of his son, Saubhadra.

sanskrit: tatrātiṣṭhan mahārājo rūpam indrasya dhārayan snuṣāṃ tāṃ pratijagrāha kuntīputro yudhiṣṭhiraḥ
english: Standing there in the form of great Indra, Yudhiṣṭhira the son of Kuntī formally received her as a daughter-in-law.

sanskrit: pratigṛhya ca tāṃ pārthaḥ puraskṛtya janārdanam vivāhaṃ kārayām āsa saubhadrasya mahātmanaḥ
english: And having received her, placing Janārdana at the fore, Pārtha caused the wedding of the great-souled Saubhadra to be performed.

sanskrit: tasmai sapta sahasrāṇi hayānāṃ vātaraṃhasām dve ca nāgaśate mukhye prādād bahu dhanaṃ tadā
english: To him he gave seven thousand swift-as-wind horses and two hundred foremost elephants and much wealth besides.

sanskrit: kṛte vivāhe tu tadā dharmaputro yudhiṣṭhiraḥ brāhmaṇebhyo dadau vittaṃ yad upāharad acyutaḥ
english: When the wedding was accomplished, then Yudhiṣṭhira the son of Dharma gave to the brahmins the wealth that Acyuta had brought.

sanskrit: gosahasrāṇi ratnāni vastrāṇi vividhāni ca bhūṣaṇāni ca mukhyāni yānāni śayanāni ca
english: Thousands of cows, jewels, garments of every kind, choice ornaments, vehicles, and couches —

sanskrit: tan mahotsavasaṃkāśaṃ hṛṣṭapuṣṭajanāvṛtam nagaraṃ matsyarājasya śuśubhe bharatarṣabha
english: That city of the Matsya king, resembling a great festival, thronged with happy and well-fed people, shone brilliantly, O bull of the Bharatas.
